summary: Official guidance allows direct upgrades without interim releases. The XF1 boundary requires replacement add-ons and rebuilt styles/templates. A matched database and file backup is needed for rollback. A real-site clone rehearsal remains necessary.
XF2 add-ons have explicit IDs, src/addons paths and addon.json metadata. legacy_addon_id maps a supported XF2 successor to its XF1 identity; it does not translate executable code.
An existing database must be converted with the supported xf:convert-utf8mb4 command before fullUnicode is set true. This should follow the core upgrade and a separate backup/test window.

The official 2.3.13 release includes security fixes. It states PHP 7.2 minimum, PHP 8.3 recommended, MySQL 5.7 minimum, and matching official add-on requirements. The supplied archive requirements.json agrees.

allowed_classes=false prevents normal application classes from being instantiated during decoding. It does not replace validation of decoded data shapes or the need to keep untrusted input away from deserialization.

The 21 October PHP advisory names critical engine vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Fixed supported releases include 8.3.36; older branches require documented vendor or exceptional source backports. Application compatibility patches do not apply these engine fixes.
